# The film's capture mode births 146 px wide vessels and the compose beat never converts

## Context

The take arm of the flagship film runs without Playwright viewport emulation: `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs#pinToCaptureDisplay` asserts `page.viewportSize()` is null before and after staging the main window at `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS`, so the recording captures a real window. In that mode the film's second-window beat reds every time; under the tour's emulated 1280×800 viewport the same script is green.

Measured 2026-09-25 on the external display (3360×1890, pin 2632,100,1320,920) at dev@f9a776c50c with the per-window sampler (a scratch spec; receipts kept in `test-results/dock-wow-demo/glitch-probe/2026-09-25/capture-mode/`), one run — the same red twice earlier today at dev@8c54e51132, receipts not kept:

- main window inner 1320×833, outer 1320×920: the pin is honoured.
- both vessels (the tear-out's and the conversion's): outer 146×239, inner 146×172, from their first sample (47 ms and 180 ms after creation) to their last; the provisional chrome fills each at 100 %, one tab strip each, no stand-in.
- `lastVesselParkReceipt` stayed null for the whole run: no park was ever proposed.
- tour receipt: `film-second-window[1] host step settlement failed: convert-while-dragging: target vessel did not reach one parked semantic + rendered claim`.
- emulated mode today, ten runs: vessels 320×240, the park lands in one attempt, the beat is green.

## The Problem

Observation and inference kept apart. Observed: a born width of 146 against a request the app floors at 320 (`VesselWorkspace#openTearOutVessel`: `width = max(round(proxyRect.width || 480), 320)`, `height = max(…, 240)`); the height came out 239 outer, so the request reached the platform, and the conversion sensor never proposed a park. Inferred: with a 146 px wide source dragged over a 146 px wide target, the pointer's grab offset inside the source moves the source rect off the target by a large fraction of the smaller extent, so `VesselConversion`'s composed ratio (overlap over the smaller extent per axis, `min(rx, ry)`) never reaches `convertThreshold` 0.55 and the sensor never proposes. Which layer narrows the width to 146 — Blink's feature parsing, Chrome's window placement on this display, or the popout boot resizing itself — is unmeasured.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs#openTearOutVessel` (~:1130): the `windowFeatures` string `height=…,left=…,top=…,width=…` with the 320×240 floor; `tearOutVesselDims` and `lastVesselOpen` record the request.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselConversion.mjs#sample` / `axisRatio`: overlap divided by the smaller extent per axis, `composeRatios = min(rx, ry)`, entry at 0.55.
- `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs#executeCrossWindowDockStep`: the pointer goes to the target's inner centre and waits for `remoteSnapshot.ready` for `attempts` frames.
- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs`: `pinToCaptureDisplay` (no emulation, the take) vs `placeNativeWindow` (the tour's emulated placement).

## The Fix

*Restated 2026-09-25 ~14:20Z by the assignee with the layer named (AC-1) and the scope cut to it; the compose beat's remaining cause moved to its own ticket.*

**The layer (measured, bare `window.open` from the pinned main window, one run in each mode):** in capture mode a popup opened with `height=240,left=3956,top=687,width=320` is born 320×239 inner / 320×306 outer — the platform honours the request. Read synchronously right after `window.open()`, the newborn answers `innerWidth 320, innerHeight 239, outerWidth 0, outerHeight 0`: it has no frame yet. `Main#windowOpen`'s `useTotalHeight` branch resizes it at exactly that moment with `resizeTo(outerWidth, innerHeight)` → `resizeTo(0, 239)`, and Chrome lands the width on its minimum: 146×239 outer, 146×172 inner — the film's vessels. Under the tour's emulation the same read answers `320×306` at once, so the resize yields 320×240 and the defect never shows. The resize itself is intentional (the window takes the size of the widget it replaces, the content a little smaller); its input was the unlaid frame instead of the request.

**The change:** `Main#windowOpen` derives the total size from the feature string (`Main.parseWindowFeatureSize`: `width`/`height` or their `inner*` spellings, both positive, else no resize) and calls `resizeTo(width, height)` with the requested numbers. Emulated and real windows now agree: 320×240 outer, the content below the title bar. No caller changes; a request that names no size is left as the platform made it.

**Not in this ticket:** with the size right, the capture-mode compose beat still reports `target vessel did not reach one parked semantic + rendered claim` — the target claims the pointer (`claimCount: 1`) but the conversion never proposes (`converted: false`, no park receipt). The born vessel's content sits one title bar (67 px) below where the pointer-follow assumes it, so the two inner rects overlap too little on the y axis for the 0.55 threshold. That is the follow's origin, not the size; it has its own ticket (see Related).

- [ ] AC-2 In capture mode on the film-stage display both vessels are born at the requested total size (320×240 outer, 320×173 inner); one headed run at the PR head, per the operator's one-run rule.
- [ ] AC-3 The tracked film arm under emulation reports no new error before its native-return beat (headless refuses that beat by construction), 3/3 headless at the PR head.
- [ ] AC-4 A unit arm drives `Main#windowOpen` with a newborn that reports no frame and asserts the resize carries the request; red on `dev`, green with the fix.

### @neo-fable - 2026-09-25T14:15:05Z

**AC-1 receipt — the layer is `Main#windowOpen`'s total-height resize reading a frameless newborn.** Bare `window.open` from the pinned main window (film stage, external display, one run per mode; `t0` = read synchronously after `window.open()`, `settled` = 1 s after load; `mimic` = the app's exact call `resizeTo(outerWidth, innerHeight)` at `t0`):

| mode | features | t0 inner / outer | mimic | settled inner / outer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| capture (no emulation, DPR 2) | `height=240,left=3956,top=687,width=320` | 320×239 / **0×0** | no | 320×239 / 320×306 |
| capture | same | 320×239 / 0×0 | yes → `resizeTo(0, 239)` | **146×172 / 146×239** |
| capture | `height=240,width=320` | 320×239 / 0×0 | yes | 146×172 / 146×239 |
| emulated (1280×800 viewport, DPR 1) | `height=240,left=3956,top=687,width=320` | 320×240 / 320×306 | no | 320×240 / 322×320 |
| emulated | same | 320×240 / 320×306 | yes → `resizeTo(320, 240)` | 320×240 / 320×240 |

So the platform honours the request; the app's resize at that instant does not have a frame to read on a real window, and Chrome lands `resizeTo(0, …)` on its minimum width, 146 px here. Under emulation the metrics answer the request at once and the same call yields 320×240, which is why the tour never showed it. The resize's intent stands (the window takes the widget's size, the content below the title bar); its input moves from the newborn's frame to the request — PR follows.

With that fixed, the capture-mode compose beat still does not settle: the driver's snapshot at the failed step reads `claimCount 1, winnerStableId workstation-vessel:metrics, converted false, engaged false, parkReceipt null` — the target claims the pointer and the conversion never proposes. Geometry at the last frame: target outer top 1148, source outer top 1286, both 320×240 outer with a 67 px title bar, so the inner rects (173 tall) overlap 35 px on y: 0.20 against the 0.55 threshold, while the outer rects would overlap 0.43. The pointer sits 15 px below the source's outer top, inside its title bar: the follow places the window's outer origin at pointer minus the grab offset, and the content is one title bar lower. Under emulation the popup's metrics carry no title bar, so the same follow lands the pointer inside the content. That is the follow origin's ticket, not this one.
